**Analysis of test image:**
- Green, mature mango leaf with irregular dark brown-black patches scattered across the surface
- Patches are irregular in shape and size, distributed across the blade (not just margins)
- Leaf veins and overall structure remain intact and green
- No white powdery coating, no raised galls, no curling/drying, no stripped stems

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Sooty Mould**: Reference shows dark irregular patches/encrustation on green leaf surfaces — closely matches the test image pattern
- **Anthracnose**: Reference shows necrosis primarily at tips/margins of young yellowish leaves — doesn't match
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Jagged brown necrotic margins with angular lesions — doesn't match
- **Gall_Midge**: Distinct raised bumps/galls on leaf surface — doesn't match
- **Die_Back**: Completely brown/withered dried leaves — doesn't match
- **Cutting_Weevil**: Stripped shoots with triangular leaf remnants — doesn't match
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White/grey powdery circular spots — doesn't match

The test image shows dark superficial irregular patches on an otherwise intact green leaf, which is characteristic of Sooty Mould growing on honeydew deposits. The pattern is a very close visual match to the Sooty Mould reference (bottom-left panel especially).

Rules out: Anthracnose (no margin-focused necrosis on young leaves), Bacterial_Canker (no angular raised lesions), Gall_Midge (no raised galls), Powdery_Mildew (no white powdery coating), Die_Back (leaf is still green), Cutting_Weevil (no stripped shoots)."}
